background: Citigroup is the holding company of the most international of the large US banks, with services, markets, banking, wealth and US personal banking as its main lines, and a multi-year restructuring behind it.
synthesis: All three of the main agencies rate the group, A- on average and BBB+ at the weakest of them, one on a positive outlook and two on stable, with no rating action since a one-notch downgrade by one of the three on 2 Dec 2015. Capital is on the weak side of US banks, CET1 of 11.8% and leverage of 5.2% both below the peer median, with leverage down 0.4 points since 30 Sep 2025. Liquidity is the stronger leg, LCR of 117% above the peer median and broadly flat, as has CET1 been (figures to 30 Jun 2026). Flagged items in the last 90 days run both ways: an improved earnings outlook on 27 Sep 2026 against a UK penalty for sanctions-control failures earlier in September, the latter a conduct cost rather than a threat to the balance sheet.
